who: Historian of Italian Renaissance diplomacy, University of Massachusetts Amherst, also affiliated with Yale; PhD Harvard.

evidence.says: The archival authority biography identifies Ilardi as a Renaissance historian with a Harvard doctorate, teaching at Massachusetts from 1957 and at Yale during 1993–2000.
LC identifies Vincent Ilardi as the author of Studies in Italian Renaissance Diplomatic History (1986).
Catalogue metadata identifies Ilardi's The Italian League and Francesco Sforza as a Harvard PhD thesis, 1958.

notes: Name, specialized works, Harvard doctorate and Yale affiliation agree. Yale teaching dates precede Dover's 2002 completion; the direct supervision was not independently located.

who: Thomas L. Karnes, historian of Latin America and history department chair at Arizona State University; PhD Stanford.

evidence.says: The News & Observer obituary states that Karnes earned his Stanford PhD in Latin American history and retired as ASU history chair in 1984 after sixteen years.
LC's Thomas L. Karnes authority cites his Los fracasos de la union (1982).
The university-press book record for William Gilpin: Western Nationalist identifies author Thomas L. Karnes as professor of history at Arizona State University.

notes: The candidate's name and field agree with the ASU historian, whose tenure includes Wilson's 1973 dissertation. Stanford institution confirmed; exact doctorate year not independently verified.

who: Edward W. Kase, ancient historian at Loyola University Chicago and director of its Phokis-Doris Expedition; PhD Loyola, winter 1972–73.

evidence.says: The obituary identifies Kase as Loyola history professor, teaching there from 1971, with a doctorate in winter 1972–73; it connects him to The Great Isthmus Corridor Route.
LC identifies Edward W. Kase from the title page of The Great Isthmus Corridor Route, the Phokis-Doris Expedition publication.
Loyola records Edward W. Kase's PhD dissertation, A Surface Exploration in Search of Mycenean Roads in Nomos Fokidhos and Nomos Fthiatidhos, with award date 1972.
Loyola records William Joseph Cherf's The Dhema Pass and Its Early Byzantine Fortifications as a history PhD dissertation awarded in 1983.

notes: The expedition publication bridges the authority and Loyola historian. Repository dates differ from AHA: Kase 1972 versus 1973, explained by winter 1972–73; Cherf 1983 versus 1984.

who: Neil Kennedy, Memorial University historian of Bermuda and the Atlantic world; PhD University of Western Ontario; supervisor of Phillip Reid.

evidence.says: Memorial identifies Kennedy as associate professor of history, specializing in seventeenth-century Bermuda and the Caribbean, with a Western Ontario PhD.
The October 2015 announcement names Neil Kennedy as supervisor of Phillip Reid's Merchant Ship Technology and the Development of the British Atlantic Empire project.
This authority identifies N. Brent Kennedy, author of The Melungeons.
The biographical notice identifies N. Brent Kennedy as holding a University of Tennessee doctorate and academic appointments at Tusculum, Mercer, Virginia's College at Wise and Georgetown.
This Neil Kennedy is a Cornish-language and university ESOL teacher, formerly a cultural studies lecturer, author of Cornish Solidarity.
This Neil Kennedy authority is established from cast credits for Sebastiane.
This authority identifies Nicholas Patrick Kennedy, author of The Tragic Isle.
This Neil Craig Kennedy is a poet and librarian with degrees in English literature, creative writing and library science, author of A Jigsaw Puzzle.

notes: The Memorial supervisor is directly established. All five candidates identify other authors or a performer; none matches his name, degree and academic career.

who: Kevin Frederic Kern, historian at the University of Akron; PhD Bowling Green State University, 1997.

evidence.says: LC identifies Kevin F. Kern with Akron's history department and T. Wingate Todd: Pioneer of Modern American Physical Anthropology; it cites his Akron CV for the full name Kevin Frederic Kern.
The 2009 graduate bulletin lists Kevin F. Kern as associate professor of history, appointed in 2001, with a Bowling Green State PhD in 1997.

notes: The LC authority explicitly matches Akron's history department, and the university confirms the exact doctorate institution and year. Other Kern candidates concern different authors or music.

who: Joseph A. Kessler, University of Kentucky historian researching Hungary and Pan-Turanism; the supplied AHA record gives a Berkeley PhD in 1967.

evidence.says: The AHA program identifies Joseph A. Kessler of the University of Kentucky presenting The Pan-Turanian Idea and Radical Neo-Nationalism in Hungary, 1890–1945.
The catalogue attributes Turanism and Pan-Turanism in Hungary, 1890–1945 to Joseph A. Kessler.
The Joseph Israel Kessler authority cites only An Era: Looking Back; it supplies no university affiliation or doctorate.
This Josef Kessler is identified with neurological research at the Max Planck Institute in Cologne.
This J. Christian Kessler is the State Department official who wrote Verifying Nonproliferation Treaties.

notes: The supervisor is identifiable as Joseph A. Kessler, but no candidate is linked to his Kentucky position or dissertation. Joseph Israel's sparse record remains unresolved; the other authorities describe different names, fields or periods.

who: Laurence Kitzan, historian of Britain and the British Empire at the University of Saskatchewan, author of Victorian Writers and the Image of Empire.

evidence.says: The publisher identifies Kitzan as Saskatchewan history faculty teaching British and imperial history, and author of Victorian Writers and the Image of Empire.
LC establishes Laurence Kitzan from Victorian Writers and the Image of Empire (2001).
The university retirees' newsletter states that Kitzan began his career in Saskatchewan's history department in 1962 and retired as professor emeritus.

notes: The identical book connects the LC authority to Saskatchewan faculty, with an appointment beginning before the student's 1971 dissertation. Toronto doctorate not independently verified.

who: H. Peter Krosby, historian of modern Europe and Nordic diplomacy, Wisconsin–Madison 1962–68, then University at Albany; PhD Columbia, 1967.

evidence.says: His CV gives a Columbia PhD in modern European history in 1967, Wisconsin–Madison employment in 1962–68 and Albany in 1968–2023; it lists Finland, Germany, and the Soviet Union, 1940–1941: The Petsamo Dispute.
LC identifies H. Peter (Hans Peter) Krosby from Finland, Germany, and the Soviet Union, 1940–1941 (1968).

notes: The exact doctorate and book establish the match. Wisconsin employment ended in 1968, before Reinertson's 1971 completion; the direct supervision was not independently located.
